expected_effect: Public val_bpb on the same-host control host decreases by 0.0004-0.0010 (predicted ~1.0053 on trn21 vs 1.005734; ~1.0055 on trn22 vs 1.005967) at essentially unchanged throughput (steps within 2% of the same-host control: >=2030 on trn21, >=2035 on trn22). Classification: SUCCESS if bpb <= control-0.0004 with steps >= 0.98x control; FALSIFIED if bpb >= control-0.0001 with steps >= 0.98x control (FP32 state math does not matter for these tables at this budget); INCONCLUSIVE if bpb lands between control-0.0004 and control-0.0001 with steps >= 0.98x control (record as null, do not adopt); CONFOUNDED per protocol section 5 if steps < 0.90x control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22), which is also recorded as a failure of the throughput prediction; steps between 0.90x and 0.98x with improved bpb is recorded as INCONCLUSIVE-throughput and may motivate a follow-up with the fused kernel, not adoption. Public and private shards differ, so only the direction is expected to transfer to the official score.
hypothesis: The default 9a4caa7b model carries 4 hashed n-gram tables of 1,048,576 rows x 128 dims stored in BF16 and trained with a flat-LR RMSProp whose second-moment state math also runs in BF16 (control ledger rows record `ngram_ve: ... opt=rmsprop flat_lr=True bf16=True rms_fp32_state_math=False nki_rms=False`). With beta2 near 1, the per-step increment (1-beta2)*g^2 is frequently smaller than 1/256 of the running state and is lost to BF16 rounding, so the RMSProp denominator for the sparsely-touched rows is biased and the effective per-row step size is erratic. Doing the RMSProp state math in FP32 (--ngram-rms-fp32) removes that quantization bias for a compute cost proportional only to the gathered rows (index_gather=True), so loss per step should improve at essentially unchanged throughput. Supporting paired evidence: fs-w3-w896-direct-control-r1 (trn21, 2026-09-18 09:18, seed 42, 2188 steps, 0.987568) vs fs-w4-w896-nki-rms-fp32-r1 (trn21, same day 09:58, same seed/shape/flags plus FP32 n-gram RMSProp, 2204 steps, 0.986947): -0.00062 BPB with +0.7% steps. Caveats acknowledged: that pair also enabled the fused NKI kernel (--nki-ngram-rms) and spans two commits (00f82d8a -> a62df273, the commit that added the feature), so it is suggestive, not isolating; it was run at width 896 under BF16 matmult autocast, not the default shape under CC='--optlevel=1'. No default-shape run with --ngram-rms-fp32 alone appears in the supplied ledger, DECISION_LOG.md, or CURRENT_STATE.md, and this direction is not among the parked ones.
single_causal_change: Pass --ngram-rms-fp32 only: RMSProp state math for the hashed n-gram value-embedding tables is performed in FP32 instead of BF16. Nothing else changes: no --nki-ngram-rms kernel switch, no table dtype change (--ngram-ve-bf16 stays at its default True), no precision/kernel/optimizer/schedule/shape flag. Launch is otherwise identical to the pinned controls: NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42, environment NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1' exactly (no autocast flags), NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, evaluated with the unchanged public evaluator settings. The matched comparison is the same-host pinned control: trn21 -> al-20260922-control-trn21-lnc2x4-9a4caa7b-full-r1 (2071 steps, 1.005734); trn22 -> al-20260922-control-trn22-lnc2x4-9a4caa7b-full-r1 (2076 steps, 1.005967).
